top_n_fasta_check.finding: MISLABELLED. In every run and both records, headers (>RNA<idx>) equal the true top-10 indices by efficacy (in ranked order), but the sequences written are always siRNA rows 0..9 in positional order (RESULT_ranked['siRNA'][i] is label-based on a RangeIndex). 8-10 of 10 entries per file have header != sequence row (matches only where a top-k row happens to have index k).
top_n_fasta_check.consequence: PITA/TargetScan scores are computed for windows pos 1-10 but merged onto the top-10-by-efficacy rows via the header name. Scores are deterministic per scored sequence (identical across runs for each actual sequence), but which rows receive them changes with the stochastic ranking, so pita_score/targetscan_score/off_target_filter/filter columns are NOT reproducible across runs (RNA0 run1 vs run2/run3 differ; RNA1 all pairs differ).

observed_hazards: Interactive input(): sequences can only be passed on stdin, and the prompts also go to stdout, so a wrapper must parse the last line.
The model path is relative ('model/mismatch_model.pth') and is loaded when scripts/mismatch.py is imported, which main.py does unconditionally, so cwd must be the OligoFormer root in every mode.
main.py creates ./result in cwd as a side effect.

The only input check is length 19: lowercase, T, N or other characters crash with a bare KeyError traceback. A wrapper should validate or uppercase the input before calling (and decide whether to convert T->U), or report the KeyError as a tool error.

Upstream behaviour, recorded and not fixed: the identical pair scores 0.991731584072113, LOWER than the 1-mismatch reference pair (0.9940418601036072). The score is a learned value and is not guaranteed to peak at 0 mismatches.
limitations: Tested only on CPU, macOS arm64.
kon is whatever the upstream model defines; upstream publishes no reference values for these pairs.
